items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: But John didn’t want to leave his family, so he said, “Why don’t you get Claude Williams?”

ctx.x: I want to just ask you a kind of final question here, is, you know you’ve seen a lot of music and played with a lot of great players. What do you see for the future of jazz? Where do you see it going? Or at least the future of jazz violin playing?

Well let me see. It’s, new things is happening every day. It’s going to be some type of a change, but I mean I couldn’t say right now what. Like I know anywhere from six to eight good violin players and they all play a different style. And even if they is going to read a sheet, they all read the same sheet, there would be a difference, because different ones would have different ways to attack the note. Because there is one, a correct way to attack, you know that they teach, and others is just another way of…
And so that kind of gave you that pit experience.
